cases.name: A triangle needs closure
cases.description: Two rising and falling strokes do not establish a closed triangular contour. A source can expose one actual three-edge cycle without specifying angles or lengths.
cases.questionPurpose: Ask whether a three-edge cycle actually exists.
cases.humanReading: A pointed outline; the base has not been reported.

cases.name: Crossing does not establish a junction
cases.description: The unjoined source has two continuous strokes with a declared crossing. The alternative has four arms sharing one actual site. Equal screen positions never create a shared site.
cases.questionPurpose: Ask for actual four-arm incidence; a negative answer rejects the joined interpretation.
cases.humanReading: Horizontal and vertical participation meet in the drawing.

cases.name: A T and a Y offer different routes
cases.description: Both candidates have a three-arm shared site. Their actual outgoing heading participation distinguishes an axial cap from a diagonal fork without assigning calibrated angles.
cases.questionPurpose: Ask which three-arm heading pattern is present.
cases.humanReading: One stem meets two arms at a common site.

cases.name: Alternating directions need not form a path
cases.description: Separate strokes can have the same placement and headings as a connected zigzag. A three-edge walk query tests the intermediate shared-site relations.
cases.questionPurpose: Ask whether three consecutive diagonal edges are actually connected.
cases.humanReading: The visible headings alternate up-right and down-right.

cases.name: Simultaneous and separated motion differ
cases.description: A zigzag combines horizontal and vertical participation within each edge. A square wave separates them into alternating axial edges. The question distinguishes the native walk, rather than a rendered bend style.
cases.questionPurpose: Ask whether an axial horizontal/vertical three-edge walk is present.
cases.humanReading: The path advances while alternately rising and falling.

cases.name: The same outline cannot reveal its recipe
cases.description: One sample is a single turning path; the other is four separate sides joined through actual public ports. Their exposed incidence and headings agree. Without a provenance service, the reader must retain both construction hypotheses.
cases.questionPurpose: Confirm the contour, then retain the recipe ambiguity; the source does not advertise ancestry.

limits: The candidates are supplied executable constructions. This is selective inquiry among known possibilities, not open-ended shape discovery or pixel recognition.
The earlier five ranking coefficients are reused unchanged. No new topology, join or heading examples train them in this run.
The source, supplier audit and post-run vocabulary comparison are separate from receiver inputs. The caption suggesting a coarse human reading is explanatory text, not a transmitted native hint.
Queries ask whether actual bounded incidence/heading patterns exist. Negative answers require completed search within the declared grammar. Incomplete or unsupported searches return open.

A valid broader question is placed first for every policy in the five distinguishing cases. It cannot separate those candidate libraries; its purpose is to check that the ranking reads actual discrimination rather than list order.

The source supplier eagerly induces its bounded motif inventory before answering. Fewer requests demonstrate selective communication; this does not yet demonstrate avoided source-side search computation.

Independent validation compares both bounded existential motif vocabularies. Agreement does not prove graph isomorphism, motif counts, translation cadence, global arrangement or construction ancestry.

The crossing case rejects a shared junction among the supplied alternatives. It does not discover the crossing position or choose over/under. The source separately carries an explicit crossing declaration.
The square recipe case intentionally keeps two alternatives. A provenance service would be needed to distinguish their generating constructions.
One existential answer publishes one matching occurrence. Other source components and occurrences stay private; the complete proof is retained only on the supplier audit surface.

Screen coordinates and angles are illustrative realizations. Solid dots indicate actual shared sites; paired hollow markers indicate different actual sites at one projected location. Rendering creates no native connections.
